$comment: Type-check only (npm run typecheck -> tsc -p tsconfig.json). Source is src/**/*.ts; the shipped lib/ and root client.js are gitignored build artifacts produced by tsdown (npm run build) — never committed, never hand-edited (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). checkJs:false means a .js/.mjs input is checked only where a top-level '// @ts-check' opts it in (test/, tsdown.config.mjs); outside this scope such a pragma is inert, so add it when adding a JS helper that should be checked. The .ts sources are always checked. Start with strict:false; raise per-module as the backlog clears. erasableSyntaxOnly is TRUE (added in ab37724 alongside verbatimModuleSyntax, where it was flipped on because it cost 0 errors — the rationale was not written down then, so it is recorded here): the suite runs on bare `node` (test/run.mjs -> node test/*.test.mjs) with no bundler, no loader and no dependencies, importing `src/host/*.ts` directly (53 such imports), so Node's strip-only loader is the real compiler for every module a test can reach. Strip-only mode cannot execute `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`) or angle-bracket assertions (`<T>expr`) — it fails at RUNTIME with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX — while plain tsc accepts all four, so without this flag a `.ts` file can typecheck clean and only explode when a suite imports it. The flag moves that to a compile-time error (TS1294). Do not drop it while the tests import sources directly; it is not a style preference and it is not about .tsx (this project has none).
